why: The SSH login hand-off also accepts a helper in the runtime folder: when the home folder cannot run programs (mounted noexec), the Mac installs the helper in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dispatch/bin/versions/<sha256>/ (grants without agent hooks only) and publishes dispatch/bin/versions/<sha256>/dispatch-helper, which the login checks as it checks the home cache (absolute $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, private folders, the file's SHA-256) before it execs that file by its physical path. For a home path the login does exactly what it did: it execs "$HOME/$helper" with the same arguments, now through a variable. Text only, so the recorded login commands are rewritten; every recorded answer still holds. Recorded observations of a running ssh's arguments (results) keep the old text, and the app only reads them.

replace.new:
cd "$HOME" || exit 1
  case "$helper" in /*) ;; *) helper="$HOME/$helper";; esac
